decision: Does TensorLBM's recorded benchmark-method-selection (oss_solutions id=417: MRT + half-way BB + far_field + quadratic sponge + Ladd MEM + Hann-FFT St, for the square-cylinder vortex-shedding benchmark) reproduce the numbers that mature OSS LBM practice selects for the same benchmark (BGK single-relaxation per Maarten-vd-Sande/lbm; TRT Lambda=3/16 per lssfau/lbmpy + lettucecfd/lettuce), within the owner 15% criterion? And which selection knobs actually carry the difference?

alternatives.A1_recorded_mrt_sponge: MRT (s_e=1.64, s_eps=1.54, s_q=1.7) + per-cell sponge tau_field (alpha=10, 6D, quadratic) -- the recorded TensorLBM selection (oss_solutions id=417)
alternatives.A2_oss_bgk_plain: BGK single relaxation + plain zero-gradient outlet -- OSS collision/outlet choice as implemented in Maarten-vd-Sande/lbm (lbm/streamcollide.py::collide uses a scalar omega; lbm/streamcollide.py::set_outlet copies the 3 upstream populations)
alternatives.A3_oss_trt_plain: TRT with magic parameter Lambda=3/16 + plain zero-gradient outlet -- OSS collision choice of lbmpy/lettuce (Ginzburg 2008)
alternatives.A4_recorded_mrt_plain: MRT + no sponge: bridge/control arm sharing everything with A1 except the sponge and with A2/A3 except the collision operator

hypothesis: H1: Cd_mean/St/Cl_amp differences between A1 (recorded) and the OSS collision choices A2/A3 stay below 15% at the same resolution, i.e. the collision-operator part of the recorded selection is not the accuracy driver; H0 (falsifier): |Delta| >= 15% on at least one KPI.

metrics.cd_mean: Fx averaged over the analysis window normalized by 0.5*rho*U^2*D (lattice units, rho=1)
metrics.st: Strouhal number from the Cl spectrum: Hann window + FFT + parabolic peak interpolation, St=f*D/U
metrics.st_zc: cross-check Strouhal from mean zero-crossing period of the windowed Cl signal
metrics.cd_std_window_frac: std(Cd)/mean(Cd) over the analysis window (periodicity check)

unit_of_analysis: one completed simulation arm at fixed (Re, blockage, D, U); KPIs are scalars per arm

baseline_control.baseline: A1 at each resolution (the recorded TensorLBM selection)
baseline_control.control: A4 (sponge off) shares everything with A1 except the absorbing layer
baseline_control.cross_implementation_note: the OSS arms are method transplants into the same kernels (identical BC / force estimator / post-processing) so the comparison isolates the collision-operator choice; a code-independent OSS run was not possible in this environment (see friction log)

predeclared_thresholds.interpretation: |KPI(arm) - KPI(A1)| / |KPI(A1)| * 100 must be < 15% for every KPI and every arm for H1 to hold
predeclared_thresholds.convergence_rule: a KPI is treated as resolution-converged when |KPI(D=14) - KPI(D=10)| / |KPI(D=14)| < 10%; otherwise the D=10 value is reported as resolution-limited and the resolution delta itself is reported as a sensitivity result
predeclared_thresholds.stability_rule: a run that produces a non-finite population or |Cl| > 10 (50x the expected O(1) amplitude) is declared failed and excluded, not tuned
predeclared_thresholds.stability_fallback: if an arm violates the stability rule at a resolution, the collision comparison is repeated at the next resolution of the predeclared ladder {10, 14, 20} (tau = 0.5+3*U*D/Re rises with D); the failing arm is reported as a measured selection-relevant failure, not silently dropped

stopping_rule: each arm runs a fixed number of steps computed before the run from St_seed and the predeclared period count (seed 2 periods + 20 shedding periods); no arm is extended or truncated after inspecting the KPIs. Wall-clock budget per arm: 900 s.
variables_controlled: statistics window (last 50% of the post-seed samples), St estimator
float64 CPU torch, fixed thread count
confounders: wall-clock truncation would bias statistics -> disabled by the predeclared fixed step count
the OSS arms re-use TensorLBM kernels, so code-level (not only method-level) differences are not covered -> declared limitation
float64 vs OSS float32 (Maarten-vd-Sande lbm/init.py uses float32) is a known confounder of the transplant, not measured separately here
2D free-stream numerical values are known to sit above 3D wind-tunnel experiments for square cylinders; the reference caliber is 2D numerical
repetition_rationale: deterministic solver: zero-variance per arm, so repetitions are replaced by (a) two resolutions, (b) four method arms, (c) two independent St estimators. Total 8 arms (4 methods x {D=10, D=14} for A1/A2, D=10 for A3/A4 plus D=14 for A1/A2).

environment.host: control container, 128 cores shared with the control plane; each arm pinned to 8 torch threads

oss_sources.Maarten-vd-Sande/lbm: ~/oss-cache/Maarten-vd-Sande_lbm @ 573a01c (BGK, Zou-He inlet, zero-gradient outlet, half-way bounce-back)
oss_sources.pylbm: ~/oss-cache/pylbm (source only, needs mpi4py/cython/h5py -> not runnable here)
oss_sources.lbmpy/lettuce: cited via oss_solutions census rows 415/416/417 (TRT magic Lambda=3/16 default)

analysis_plan: for each KPI: table arm x resolution with % difference vs A1 (same D) and vs converged value; H1 verdict by the predeclared 15% rule; uncertainty = resolution delta + St cross-estimator spread; no post-hoc threshold changes.

comparison_logic.sponge_effect: A1 vs A4 (single difference: absorbing layer)
comparison_logic.collision_effect: A4 vs A2 vs A3 (single difference: collision operator, identical BC/outlet/force/post-processing)
comparison_logic.recorded_vs_oss: A1 vs A2/A3 (both knobs, i.e. the real-world selection difference)
